rv.q: This production’s standout actors, anchored by Belcher, could make you think otherwise.
Tata’s staging takes many counterintuitive tacks here, several of them orthogonal to the play itself.
But the lack of compelling performances renders this complex tragedy, and its conflicted central character, frustratingly flat and stubbornly unengaging.
You don’t need gimmicks when your cast is this good.
The cast of Coriolanus anchors a production that, while visually striking and engaging, has little of its own insights to offer.
The greater disappointment is the director’s slack, unimaginative shaping of the crucial scenes involving those so-swayable Roman people, who collectively become the drama’s motivating force.
The production’s most problematic aspect, however, is the video and projection design by Lisa Renkel and Possible.
Tata never achieves a steady flow to the narrative; instead it stops and starts, with bumps and lags that drag it down.

cn.t: Mixed reviews for this multimedia-heavy production, with critics divided on whether the tech-forward approach enhances or distracts from Shakespeare's political tragedy about pride and power.
